children: Shares of J.B. Hunt Transport Services
were under pressure Tuesday after a company executive said recent storms in the southwest had negatively impacted its shipping volumes.

Severe flooding in New Mexico and Arizona in late October damaged railroad infrastructure along Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railway (BNSF) routes and disrupted shipping along a key freight route between Southern California and the Midwest. This impacted more than 150 trains across BNSF’s system, and although BNSF had trains moving in two and a half days, the delays continued to reverberate through the intermodal system, leaving shippers with at least a week of delays.
According to container-tracking data from RailState, J.B. Hunt
had the largest share of waiting intermodal containers.

This disruption “impacted our business on our transcon to the tune of about 7,500 loads,” J.B. Hunt Transport Executive Vice President Spencer Frazier said at a conference on Tuesday, comments which drove shares as much as 3.4% lower.
